title: add vpc control plane terraform multi-az interface endpoints peering route53
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: enable private control plane deployments to provision multi-AZ VPCs with interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 private hosted zone peering via Terraform. This change adds an opinionated, reusable module and upgrade hooks to support both fresh installs and in-place upgrades for Private (VPC) control planes.

What: single Terraform module and examples that provision: multi-AZ private subnets, NAT/route configuration, interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/ECR/STS/SecretsManager, security group templates (control-plane-only and inter-service), VPC peering resources including cross-account acceptance, Route53 private hosted zone association & peering records, and optional interface endpoint policy attachments. Includes: - conditional resources for single-AZ vs multi-AZ installs - upgrade hooks to migrate legacy single-AZ stacks to multi-AZ subnets - careful dependency ordering and apply-time timeouts for peering and Route53 association

Why: customers running Redwood Private need a repeatable, tested Terraform path to create the control-plane network. Previously we had one-off scripts and Helm chart post-install hooks; this centralizes infra for long-term maintenance and consistent security controls.

Changes: See commits for breakdown. This is a backward-compatible addition: all new behavior is opt-in via module variables. The module includes examples for AWS cross-account peering used by Dedicated and Private customers.

Testing & validation: applied against a staging AWS account (three AZs) and exercised installer: - terraform plan/apply for fresh install - terraform plan for upgrade path from single-AZ to multi-AZ (migration hooks validated) - Route53 peering verified with test DNS records and resolution between accounts - integration e2e run of private-installer that provisions control-plane and joins a private agent - automated terraform fmt and validate checks in CI - acceptance tests added to perf-canary running basic API health checks after network provisioning

Rollback/upgrade notes: - Upgrade path implemented as two-phase change with non-destructive resource creation followed by optional traffic migration. - Rollback documented in examples/upgrade-rollback.md and tied to Linear task for manual validation steps.

CI: terraform fmt/validate, unit tests for module with terratest harness, and installer e2e smoke tests. See ci_status below.

Related: Linear ENG-2147, ENG-1982; will be referenced by private-installer and helm upgrade PRs.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with examples (examples/aws-multi-az) - [x] Acceptance tests and terratest harness - [x] Upgrade/rollback example and docs - [x] README and variables documented - [x] CI integration
